passage:
'Irfan, can I tell you something? Don't laugh.'
'Okay.'
'I'm scared of dogs. Like, properly. That's why I take the long way to tuition.'
'That's it? Fine. I won't tell.'
Two weeks later, on the same tuition steps:
'Abhinav, bhai, you're quiet today.'
'Did you tell anyone? About the dogs?'
'No. Why would I?'
'Nobody's said anything. In Class 7 I told Gaurav I liked someone, and by lunch the whole class was singing her name at me. I still don't talk to him.'
'That's rough.'
'Yeah.' Abhinav picked at his bag strap. 'So there's something else. Papa wants me to keep going to the cricket academy. I hate it. I haven't told anyone.'
'Not even your mum?'
'Not even her.'
Irfan nodded slowly. 'Okay. That stays here too.'
'Thanks,' Abhinav said, and let out a long breath.

qa.q: Why does Abhinav take the long way to tuition?
qa.a: He's scared of dogs, properly, so he takes the long way to tuition.

qa.q: Why did Abhinav ask whether Irfan had told anyone about the dogs?
qa.a: He wanted to check whether the small secret had stayed private before trusting Irfan with something bigger, because of what Gaurav did.

qa.q: What was Abhinav's turning point in deciding to share more, and was it wise?
qa.a: Finding out that nobody had heard about the dogs gave him evidence Irfan could keep a secret, so sharing the cricket academy worry step by step was sensible.

qa.q: How might Irfan feel about being trusted with the cricket academy secret?
qa.a: Irfan probably feels trusted and a bit responsible, knowing Abhinav hasn't even told his mum.

grounding: A teenage boy tells a new friend a small secret first, checks it stayed private, then shares a bigger one, still wary because of an old friend's breach.

passage: When I moved to the new school in Class 9, I didn't tell anyone anything for months. In Class 8, my best friend had read my diary aloud at a sleepover, and even now I can hear everyone laughing. Then there was Pankaj, who sat next to me in chemistry. He was funny and kind, but kind people can still talk. So I tested him. I told him I can't swim, and that I get out of every pool trip by saying I have a cold. Small, embarrassing, nothing huge. I waited. A pool trip came and went, and nobody teased me. Pankaj even said, 'Uma, want to skip together and eat chaat?' A month later I told him the real thing, that my parents were separating. He listened and didn't tell a soul. I'm glad I went slowly. I'm also glad I didn't stop at the first step.

qa.q: What small secret did Uma tell Pankaj first?
qa.a: Uma told him about not being able to swim and getting out of every pool trip by saying it was a cold.

qa.q: Why was Uma so careful about telling Pankaj anything?
qa.a: Uma still remembered the Class 8 best friend reading the diary aloud at a sleepover, and feared being laughed at again.

qa.q: What choice after the pool trip showed Uma's approach working?
qa.a: After nobody teased Uma, the small test had passed, so Uma chose to share the bigger thing about the parents separating.

qa.q: How might Pankaj feel if he learned the swimming secret had been a test?
qa.a: He might feel a little surprised, but probably understanding, since he later saw why Uma needed to be sure before sharing something so big.

grounding: A teenager looks back on testing a new friend with a small secret after an old betrayal, then sharing a bigger one once it stayed private.

passage:
Counsellor's note, girls' hostel, Class 11, Rehana:
Rehana came to see me today, calmer than in her first term. She said that when she joined, she didn't trust anyone because a friend at her old school had spread her marks around. With her roommate Zainab, she tried something small first. She told Zainab she still sleeps with a torch on, and then watched for a week to see if it got around. It didn't. Last week she told Zainab that her father has lost his job, which she had kept to herself for months. She said Zainab 'just listened and made tea'. I told Rehana her careful steps made sense and asked how she was coping at home with the news. We will meet again next Thursday.

qa.q: What small thing did Rehana first tell Zainab?
qa.a: She told Zainab she still sleeps with a torch on.

qa.q: Why did Rehana watch for a week after telling Zainab about the torch?
qa.a: She wanted to be sure the small secret stayed private before trusting Zainab with more, because an old friend had spread her marks.

qa.q: How did the counsellor respond, and why was it a good next step?
qa.a: The counsellor told Rehana her careful steps made sense and asked how she was coping with the news, keeping support going with another meeting.

qa.q: How might Zainab have felt when Rehana told her about her father's job?
qa.a: Zainab likely felt trusted and wanted to comfort Rehana, which is why she just listened and made tea.

grounding: A counsellor notes how a hostel girl, hurt before, tested her roommate with a small secret and only later shared a bigger one.

passage:
Thursday
Experiment update. Two weeks ago I told Dilnaz something small: that I can't ride a cycle, at fifteen. Not a huge secret. But if it got round, the boys in our class would never let it go.
I waited. Nothing. On Monday Rohit made cycle jokes about someone else, and Dilnaz just looked at me and said nothing. Not a wink, not a hint. Nothing!
So today in the library I told her the real one: about Papa losing his job, and why I've stopped going to the canteen. She listened, then asked if I wanted to share her tiffin, and didn't make it weird.
I know it's strange to test a friend. But last year Megha told the whole class about my braces photo within a day, and I still think about it. This time I went slowly. It worked.
Sharmila

qa.q: What small secret did Sharmila tell Dilnaz first?
qa.a: That Sharmila can't ride a cycle, at fifteen.

qa.q: Why did Sharmila want to test Dilnaz with a small secret first?
qa.a: Sharmila was still hurt by Megha spreading the braces photo last year, and wanted proof Dilnaz could keep something private before trusting more.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the library, and why did it feel safe?
qa.a: After two weeks of silence about the cycle, Sharmila shared the real worry about Papa's job; Dilnaz had already shown she could keep quiet, so the bigger step felt safe.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz feel on learning she had been tested?
qa.a: Dilnaz might be a little surprised but could understand, given how Sharmila had been hurt before, and might feel glad to have earned the trust.

grounding: A teenager shares a small secret with a new friend to see if it stays private, and only then shares a bigger one, still remembering an old breach.

passage:
In Swati's small town, news travelled faster than the morning bus. So when Keerthana joined the school in July, Swati was careful. On the walk past the sugarcane fields she tested her: "Don't tell anyone, but I still can't ride a cycle."
Then she watched. A week passed. Nobody laughed at her in class, nobody at the tuition centre asked about cycles. Keerthana even offered to hold the seat and teach her near the temple ground, early, when no one was around.
Two weeks later, sitting on the canal wall, Swati told her the real thing: her father might move the family to the city after Diwali, and she hadn't told anyone else.

qa.q: What small secret did Swati tell Keerthana first?
qa.a: That she still can't ride a cycle.

qa.q: What was Swati feeling during the week after telling the cycle secret?
qa.a: She was wary and a little anxious, watching to see if it would spread in a town where news travels fast.

qa.q: Why was testing with a small secret a sensible step?
qa.a: It let Swati check Keerthana's discretion at low cost before sharing something that mattered more.

qa.q: How might Keerthana feel when she hears the bigger secret?
qa.a: She may feel trusted and a little honoured, and aware she must keep it safe.

grounding: Shows a teenager testing a new friend with a minor secret and only sharing something bigger once it stayed private.

passage:
At his new school in Melbourne, Wei had a rule: small secrets first. So at lunch he told Abebe, the boy from chemistry, "Honestly, I can't stand the band everyone's obsessed with." It was a tiny thing.
By Friday, three people in the group chat were teasing him about it. Abebe apologised. "I only told one person. I didn't think it mattered."
It didn't, really. Wei laughed it off. But he noticed he didn't tell Abebe about his parents' arguments, or about the scholarship form he was scared to send. Months later, when they were friendly again, Wei still paused every time before saying anything that mattered.

qa.q: What small secret did Wei tell Abebe?
qa.a: That he can't stand the band everyone's obsessed with.

qa.q: Why did Wei keep the bigger worries from Abebe?
qa.a: Wei felt wary and let down after the small secret spread, so the trust needed for bigger things wasn't there.

qa.q: What could Abebe do to rebuild trust with Wei?
qa.a: Keep small confidences private over a long stretch and stop treating Wei's words as harmless to pass on.

qa.q: How might Abebe see the leak?
qa.a: Abebe thinks it was tiny and harmless, not realising it was the test that decides what Wei shares next.

grounding: Shows a teenager testing a new friend with a small secret, and how one small breach is remembered long afterwards.

passage:
At the district swimming club, Elizabeth had watched the new boy, Pankaj, for a month before she tested him. On the bench after practice she said quietly, "I'm scared of the high board. That's why I always 'forget' my goggles on diving day."
Then she waited. Coach didn't hear about it. The older girls didn't tease her. On diving day Pankaj just handed her a spare pair of goggles and said, "Low board with me?"
Three weeks later, drying her hair in the corridor, she told him what she hadn't told anyone at the club: she was thinking of leaving swimming for the school quiz team, and her mother would be upset.

qa.q: What did Elizabeth always "forget" on diving day?
qa.a: Her goggles.

qa.q: How did Elizabeth feel while waiting after telling her secret?
qa.a: She felt cautious and a little nervous, unsure whether Pankaj would keep it or spread it.

qa.q: What does Pankaj's response show about how trust grows?
qa.a: By keeping the secret and quietly helping, he passed the small test, which made it safe for Elizabeth to share more.

qa.q: How might Pankaj feel when Elizabeth tells him about leaving swimming?
qa.a: He may feel trusted and a little worried for her, knowing she hasn't told anyone else at the club.

grounding: Shows a teenager at a swimming club sharing a minor secret to test a new friend before trusting him with something bigger.

passage:
Dear Didi,
You asked about my new friend, Rekha. I like her a lot. But I'm being careful.
Last week I told her one small secret: that I'm scared of dogs. It's not a big deal. I just wanted to see if she'd tell anyone.
She didn't. Nobody teased me. She even walked me the long way round the colony dog.
So yesterday I told her something bigger: that I don't want to take science next year, even though Papa wants me to. She listened. She said, "That's yours to tell, not mine."
I still remember how Anu told the whole class about my crush in Class 7. It took me a year to trust anyone after that.
Arohi

qa.a: Arohi told Rekha about being scared of dogs.

qa.q: Why did Arohi tell Rekha a small secret first?
qa.a: Arohi felt cautious and wary after being betrayed before, so Arohi wanted to test Rekha with something small.

qa.q: What does Arohi's approach show about building trust?
qa.a: Trust grows in steps: sharing a small secret first, seeing it kept, then sharing something bigger.

qa.q: How might Rekha feel if she knew she was being tested?
qa.a: Rekha might feel a little surprised, but also understand and feel trusted when Arohi shared more.

grounding: Shows a teenager testing a new friend with a small secret before sharing more, remembering an old betrayal.

passage:
You want to know how I trust people? I'm Nazia, and I do it slowly.
When Rajni joined our class, we started walking home together. After a month, I told her something small: I failed my first maths test in Class 8 and hid it from Ammi. Not a huge secret. Just a test.
I waited. A week. Two weeks. Nobody mentioned it. So I told her something bigger: that my parents argue a lot and I hate being at home some evenings.
She listened, and she said, "Want to study at my place when it's bad?"
I learned this from Class 6, when my old friend told everyone I cried at the film. You don't forget that.

qa.q: What small secret did Nazia tell Rajni first?
qa.a: Nazia failed the first maths test in Class 8 and hid it from Ammi.

qa.q: How does Nazia feel about trusting new people?
qa.a: Nazia feels cautious and careful, still remembering an old friend's betrayal.

qa.q: Why is Nazia's slow approach wise?
qa.a: Testing trust with a small secret first lets Nazia see if Rajni keeps it before sharing something that matters more.

qa.q: How might Rajni feel when Nazia tells her about home?
qa.a: Rajni might feel trusted and caring, offering Nazia a place to study.

grounding: Shows a teenager testing a new friend with a small secret before sharing a bigger one, after an old betrayal.

passage:
Week 1: Zainab and Shankar became lab partners. Zainab told him one small thing: she was nervous about the Bunsen burner. Shankar didn't laugh or tell anyone.
Week 3: Zainab told him something bigger: she was applying for a science scholarship and didn't want the class to know in case she failed. Shankar nodded. "Okay."
Week 5: In the corridor, a classmate asked Zainab, "Heard you're trying for some scholarship?" Zainab's stomach dropped. Shankar had told a friend, who told others.
Week 8: Shankar was still her lab partner. He'd said sorry twice. She was polite to him. But she never told him anything important again.

qa.q: What was Zainab nervous about in week 1?

qa.q: What was Zainab feeling when the classmate asked about the scholarship?
qa.a: She felt shocked and betrayed, with her stomach dropping as she realised Shankar had told.

qa.q: What could Shankar do to rebuild trust?
qa.a: Keep every small confidence from now on for a long time, without pushing Zainab to forgive quickly.

qa.q: How might Shankar feel by week 8?

grounding: Shows a teenager building trust in steps with a new friend, and a single breach being remembered for a long time.

passage: Nikita, you're asking how to know if a new friend can be trusted? Let me tell you how your Irawati Aaji did it, when I was a schoolgirl of fifteen. A new girl, Leena, joined our class. I liked her, but I didn't know her. So I told her one small thing: that I was scared of the school's big dog. It wasn't a great secret. I waited to see if it went round. A week passed. Nobody barked at me in the corridor. So I told her a bigger thing, that my father was ill. She kept that too. Years later another girl told someone my small secret, just once. I never trusted her again. Small tests, Nikita. Then bigger ones.

qa.q: How did young Irawati feel when a week passed and nobody barked at her?

qa.q: How might Leena have felt when Irawati shared the bigger secret?
qa.a: Leena may have felt trusted and closer to Irawati, sensing the friendship growing.

passage: It was exam week in the noisy hostel, and Irfan barely knew his new roommate, Damini's cousin, Karan. Only Damini, who shared lab bench with him, had begun to feel like a friend. Between revision sessions, with drills from the building work next door, Irfan tested her. "Don't tell anyone, but I still sleep with a night light." He watched to see if it spread. Two days passed. Nobody teased him. Karan didn't hint at anything. On Friday, Irfan told Damini something much harder: that his father's shop had closed and he might have to leave the hostel. She listened and said, "That stays with me." He believed her, because the night light had.

qa.q: What small secret did Irfan tell Damini first?
qa.a: That he still sleeps with a night light.

qa.q: Why did Irfan feel able to tell Damini about his father's shop?
qa.a: He felt safer and more trusting, because the small secret had stayed private for two days.

qa.q: What does Irfan's approach show about building trust?
qa.a: Sharing something small first and watching whether it stays private lets trust grow step by step.

qa.q: How might Damini feel being trusted with the harder news?
qa.a: Damini may feel honoured and protective, knowing Irfan chose her to share something painful.

grounding: Illustrates a teenager testing a new friend with a minor secret before sharing something bigger.

passage: Darshan had only known Ojas for a month, since he moved into the next block. One evening, cycling round the colony, Darshan tested him with something small. "Don't laugh, but I still can't swim." "I won't tell," Ojas promised. The next day at the pool party, two boys shouted, "Darshan, want a float?" and laughed. Ojas looked away. Darshan's face burned. It was such a small thing, but he felt stupid for telling. For the rest of the year, Ojas tried to be friendly, saving him a seat, lending him comics. Darshan was polite. He never told Ojas anything important again. Even when Ojas apologised, something had closed, and it stayed closed a long time.

qa.q: What small secret did Darshan tell Ojas?
qa.a: That he still can't swim.

qa.q: What did Darshan feel when the boys shouted about a float?
qa.a: He felt humiliated and betrayed, and foolish for having trusted Ojas.

qa.q: What could Ojas do to rebuild trust over time?
qa.a: He could admit plainly what he did, keep other confidences reliably, and accept that trust will return slowly if at all.

qa.q: How might Ojas feel when Darshan stays only polite?
qa.a: Ojas likely feels regretful and shut out, realising one slip cost him a real friendship.

grounding: Shows a teenager testing a new friend with a small secret, and how a single breach is remembered for a long time.

passage:
'You didn't tell anyone,' Dhruv said, as the dhol started up again on the society lawn. It was the ninth night of Navratri.
'Tell anyone what?'
'About the garba. That I've been practising the steps in my room with the door locked.'
Vaibhav shrugged. 'You asked me not to.'
'In Class 7 I told Kabir I still slept with the light on. By lunch the whole class knew.' Dhruv pulled at his kurta sleeve. 'I still don't talk to him.'
'That was two years ago.'
'Yeah. Well.' Dhruv watched the dancers circle. 'So I told you a small thing first. On the first night. To see.'
'A test?' Vaibhav laughed. 'Did I pass?'
'You passed.' Dhruv took a breath. 'Papa might be moving to Pune for work. I haven't told anyone.'
Vaibhav stopped laughing. 'Okay. I'm listening.'

qa.q: What small thing did Dhruv tell Vaibhav on the first night?
qa.a: That he had been practising the garba steps in his room with the door locked.

qa.q: What is Dhruv feeling when he brings up Kabir?
qa.a: He still feels hurt and wary, because Kabir spread a private thing to the whole class two years ago, and that one breach has stayed with him.

qa.q: Was Dhruv's small test a sensible way to build a new friendship? Why?
qa.a: Yes; sharing something minor first let him check that Vaibhav kept it private before risking something that really mattered, like the news about Papa.

qa.q: If you were Vaibhav, how might it feel to learn you had been tested?
qa.a: Maybe a bit surprised at first, which is why Vaibhav laughs, but then glad to be trusted, and ready to take the bigger news seriously 🙂
